answer: After a delinquent tax suit ends, the county sells the property at a tax sale ordered by the court for cash, subject to the taxpayer's right of redemption.
quote: After the conclusion of the delinquent tax suit, the county holds a tax sale to sell property in order to collect delinquent taxes. ... The court shall order the sale of the property for cash, subject to the equity of redemption

answer: Redemption runs from the order confirming the sale: one year if taxes were delinquent five years or less, 180 days if more than five but less than eight years, and 90 days if eight years or more.
quote: If the period of delinquency is five years or less, the redemption period shall be one year from the entry of the order confirming the sale; If the period of delinquency is more than five years but less than eight years, the redemption period shall be one hundred eighty days from the entry of the order confirming the sale; or If the period of delinquency is eight years or more, the redemption period shall be ninety days

answer: A tax deed or an order confirming the sale is an assurance of perfect title; it can be invalidated only on grounds set by statute, such as proof that the land was not liable to sale for taxes or that the taxes were paid before the sale.
quote: A tax deed of conveyance or an order confirming the sale is an assurance of perfect title to the purchaser of such land, and no such conveyance will be invalidated in any court, except by proof that the land was not liable to sale for taxes, or that the taxes for which the land was sold have been paid before the sale
